notes.title: This game is now completely free!
notes.content:
It's been a while since Camp W was released. We figure that everyone who might buy it has already bought it, but we still want it to be experienced by as many players as possible.

That's why we've made the game [b]completely free[/b]! This is the full retail copy of the game with all content and achievements available. Please download it, play it, enjoy it, and pass it on.

Since launching Camp W, we then went on to make more games -- maybe you've heard of them? Hits like [i]I Love You, Colonel Sanders! A Finger Lickin’ Good Dating Simulator[/i] and [i]Hooked on You: A Dead by Daylight Dating Sim[/i]. 

Now's your chance to see how we got our start making dating sims, the first one we ever made before we became so terminally horny that we went on to bring you sexy Colonel Sanders, Trapper, Huntress and more.

notes.title: Tales from the making of Camp W
notes.content:
We've had a few interviews go online the the past couple of weeks that you might find interesting...

[url=https://geekandsundry.com/hold-onto-the-last-magical-vestiges-of-summer-in-camp-w/]In this interview with Geek & Sundry[/url], narrative director Alexei and creative director Kelly discuss the story behind the development of Camp W's world and art style.

Here's a quote from Kelly: "I wanted to spark in people the feelings of curiosity and playfulness and acceptance and strength. With the goal that anyone could find pieces they related to somewhere in it. I wanted to make people feel good about who they are. Who they genuinely are. That they don’t need to hide, and that their choices do matter. I believe that that is a really powerful thing which could be scary, but is so exciting."

[url=http://gamasutra.com/view/news/324805/How_Camp_Ws_choicedriven_design_was_shaped_by_a_new_narrative_tool.php/]Over on Gamasutra[/url], Alexei is joined by lead engineer Charlie to discuss their new narrative game design tool, Branching Storywriter, and what it's like making an all-ages game.

Here's a snippet from that: “My worries for this particular game were sort of a genre worry, in that I feel like we’re doing something that other people aren’t doing, and you have to question, when you walk down that path, why hasn’t anybody been walking down this path before?” says Bochenek. “Is it dangerous? Or is it simply undiscovered?”

Follow each link to read the full articles.

notes.title: Unknown Pleasures: Simply the Best Five New Indies on Steam
notes.content:
The grim prospect of shopping for PC components looms over my August like a looming, grim prospect. God I love writing.

You might be surprised how demanding indie games can be on a slightly creaky video card, and not always because of ongoing optimisation. Although admittedly it’s more likely the searing heat rather than some bad code that baked my video card and almost the PSU too. Bah. That said, today’s Unknown Pleasures coincidentally has a rather low-fi theme, so let’s take a moment to thank the gods of the PC for putting an end to the hardware wars.

Mastering the basics this week: titchy interplanetary farmers, non-irritating children, and stabby jabby ninjas.

notes.title: Spooky Campfire Stories
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32602886/547cfc553041f67bedb0c6c4f5a1bc9ec72b4efe.jpg[/img]

We mentioned "Memories" in our last update, but I wanted to go a bit deeper into how exactly they work and what they contain.

One of my favorite examples of the Memory system is the telling of ghost stories, an event that happens twice in the game. Each time this happens, the campers gather late at night, and you are given three choices of which story to hear. For instance, you might get to choose between a forlorn fiancee, a mad scientist, or a creeping shadow man. Once you have chosen, another camper steps up to center stage and tells you the story, in their personal voice.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32602886/06cbe218c444a741571d5bf644f6abe709ec29ba.jpg[/img]

At the end of the story, you open up your Grimoire and sketch what you think the character looks like. On your next time through the game, you might choose a different ghost story, told by a different camper, resulting in a different Memory.

All of our Memories, of which there are dozens to collect, were done by talented illustrator [url=http://www.juliairedale.com/] Julia Iredale[/url].

notes.title: Witchy summer visual novel/adventure Camp W is out now
notes.content:
I reckon I may have a soft spot for weird summer-camp stories, if my love of Gravity Falls (technically not a camp, but hush) and Psychonauts is anything to go by. Camp W definitely fits the bill, telling the story of a young witch (gender of your choosing) spending summer at camp amongst the less magically inclined folk. There’s some snappy writing, some genuinely charming cartoon art, and while ostensibly a visual novel, there’s a bit more to do than just clicking through the story and enjoying the ride.

(more…)

notes.title: You Must Remember This
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32602886/86ef494cd1e130d7cd75f0c1b3e305255983348a.png[/img]

Throughout each playthrough of Camp W, you will unlock various "Memories." These are unique pieces of art associated with choices that [i]you[/i] make. Your Memories are stored in your Grimoire, either sketched, painted, or taped onto the page next to the character they remind you of.

Above, you can see some of Wilfred's Memories.

Each playthrough will allow you to unlock 12 different Memories, from a selection of over 60. You'll have to go through the full game more than a couple times to see them all!

notes.title: A Double Dose of Family
notes.content:
Today we've got two new characters to meet: your mom and grandma! You literally wouldn't even exist without them, which isn't something that you get to say very often.

Meet Mila and Gadgy, your loving and maybe at times a teensy bit overbearing family.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32602886/0ad6d4421afc53903a6ba123a93e3fa9fef4c688.jpg[/img]

A celebrity Witch and star of her own show on PotionTV, Mila holds you to a very high standard, but only because she knows you're capable of greatness.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32602886/7f0868206c07dac95fee235d262b3d7de102e237.jpg[/img]

Gadgy is the definition of old school cool. She's perhaps the wisest Witch you'll ever meet, not to mention the best hugger in the whole town of Coventry.

notes.title: Your Camp W History Tutor Has Arrived
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32602886/d3bfe8279590374125a63a62eadc7e01b80c4bac.jpg[/img]

There's one more character to meet at Camp W, and it just so happens that she is the most downright campery of all the campers!

Ruby is an expert on the history and lore of Camp W. Basically, she knows everything there is to know about this place--or at least she thinks she does--and she’s going to share it with you, whether you want to hear it or not!

If you want to ask her any questions, you can usually find her in the Camp History Center.

Stay tuned for more art shares, character intros, and Camp W announcements.

Next up: The counselors!

Is there such a thing as too smart for your own good? Genius twins Ella & Ezzi will certainly put that theory to the test when they attempt to repurpose the old radio tower to broadcast a signal into deep space. But when someone--or something--reaches back from the dimensional void... will you be there to answer?

notes.title: Hello New Campers!
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32602886/d94dc244d27a89bf4a863109653f01ee7cb44721.jpg[/img]

[b]We're so excited to launch Camp W this summer![/b] In the coming days and weeks we'll be sharing a lot of info and artwork on Steam as well as on [url=http://twitter.com/campw]Twitter[/url] and [url=http://twitter.com/campw]Facebook[/url]. You can also visit our website at [url=http://CampWGame.com/]CampWGame.com[/url].

In Camp W, you play as Liliandra or Lysander (your choice), a young Witch who is trespassing in the Human Realm to escape summer studies and attend sleepaway camp instead.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32602886/47727390becd69db6291196045d09644c280d542.png[/img]

[i](And yes, you can rename yourself whatever you'd like)[/i]

Over the course of the game, which encompasses the first three days of summer, you'll meet a variety of campers, each with their own story to tell. However, you won't be able to hear all the stories on a single playthrough. 

With gameplay similar to a Visual Novel--[i]we call it a "Friending Sim"[/i]--you 'll have to decide who to focus your attention on and choose to join them at their favorite activities if you want to learn more about them.

So, who are these campers you'll be meeting?

[b]Let's meet one! This is Sophie.[/b] Sophie is shy, but it doesn't take too much to get her talking. While Human kids don't know that the true Witching Realm exists, they still know about Witches from popular culture, and Sophie is a big fan of all things Witchy.

Take a look at the poses that represent Sophie's moods, posted above, which you'll see throughout your conversations with her

That's it for now, but please keep checking back! And if you like what you see, connect with us on social or tell us what you think in the forums here on Steam. See you this summer!
